::: {.callout-note title="CONVERGING candidate contract"}
Both backends provide one solver-specific `EigenmodeSim` with surface, bulk,
and port/junction EPR analysis. Their preparation and result types remain
backend-owned. Offline film reanalysis uses recorded result evidence and does
not reopen a solver. This page documents the current candidate; it does not
claim V1 stability. The [Backend Support Matrix](backend-support.qmd) separates
the implemented candidate from the currently documented exercise evidence and
limits.
:::

## Workflow and state contract {#workflow-and-state-contract}

Both backends consume a shared prepared source snapshot, but their preparation,
request and result types remain backend-owned. Ordinary modes need no film-loss
request. Surface, bulk and port/junction EPR extend a configured physical model;
output selection does not remove modeled domains or change normalization.

Learn the operations in [Palace Eigenmode](course/palace-eigenmode.qmd),
[Palace EPR](tutorial-xmon-palace.qmd), [AEDT EPR](tutorial-xmon-aedt.qmd) and
[offline reanalysis](course/offline-epr.qmd). Exact signatures and selections
belong to the [Palace Eigenmode contract](specs/palace-eigenmode.qmd) and
[AEDT contract](specs/aedt-runtime.qmd). AEDT saved-field evaluation is a native
workcopy operation; reanalysis of a recorded JSON result is offline arithmetic.

The source envelope does not equalize backend exterior conditions: unspecified
Palace Eigenmode uses natural PMC, while current AEDT EPR records HFSS default
Perfect E. Record boundary choice, Region size and numerical controls when
comparing physical models; no automatic harmonization is implied.

## Quantities and normalization {#quantities-and-normalization}

The reported participation for a supported energy numerator is

$$
p_i = \frac{U_i}{U_{norm}}.
$$

AEDT's denominator combines the unique electric-domain field energy and
declared junction capacitive energy. Palace obtains its normalization from
final native electric-domain and capacitive-energy tables. Thin-film estimates are numerator estimates; SCGSim does not add
them back into either backend's denominator. The detailed AEDT MA/MS/SA
surface formulas, material-side binding, and linearized junction normalization
are documented in [the AEDT Eigenmode reference](specs/aedt-runtime.qmd#surface-estimates-and-junction-normalization).

AEDT bulk-domain participation divides that domain's electric field energy by
the same denominator; exact field-energy formulas belong to the linked runtime
contract.
The report presents surface, bulk, and junction/port partitions on separate
axes; these views do not assert that every physical loss channel has been
evaluated.

For an AEDT planar junction, the source declaration includes its polygon,
terminal nets A and B, directed in-plane unit vector, width, inductance, and
capacitance. The formal area-average voltage and nonnegative inductive and
capacitive participation follow the convention in the linked reference.
Palace's `layout_sheet=True` port is a separate backend contract: it binds an
authored component port to a layer and inductance, then reports Palace's signed
native port participation. The signed value is phase-convention dependent and
is not the same quantity as AEDT's nonnegative $p_L$ or $p_C$.

## Surface identity, masks, and loss assumptions {#surface-identity-masks-and-loss-assumptions}

For AEDT, each `SurfaceEprSpec` binds one contribution ID and source polygon ID
to an interface (`MA`, `MS`, or `SA`), a top/bottom field side, film thickness,
film permittivity, optional loss tangent, source, preset, and alternative mask
margins. `MA` means metal-air, `MS` metal-substrate, and `SA` substrate-air.
The `field_side` records the requested top/bottom side, and the adjacent source
domains and physical owner remain explicit evidence; none is inferred from a
display label. AEDT binds a native material side using its normal-based rule.
Its `effective_domain_id` remains binding metadata rather than a solver-domain
restriction or proof that the selected field belongs to that material. `MM`
may remain semantic evidence but is not a dielectric-film energy contribution.
Surface construction requires thickness and permittivity for MA/MS/SA. At
initial AEDT configuration, interface defaults fill unspecified optional loss
and provenance fields on valid contributions; explicit per-contribution
values, including an explicit zero loss tangent, take precedence. Defaults
cannot make an incomplete spec valid.

AEDT Surface EPR integrates horizontal top/bottom support only. It does not
calculate sidewall film energy. Its unmasked baseline and every requested
margin are separate evaluations; even a caller's explicit zero margin is a
separate row. Margins are alternatives, not additive bands. Empty physical
intersection is recorded as a geometric zero. Palace retains its native
surface and mask identities; when sidewalls were not selected, their energy
remains uncomputed rather than zero.

Film loss conversion is $Q^{-1}_i=p_i\tan\delta_i$. A missing loss tangent
means unknown and yields an unavailable inverse-Q contribution; an explicit
`0.0` is a known zero and yields a zero contribution. Offline reanalysis applies
partial updates in this order: recorded assumptions, interface defaults, then
group overrides. A later value replaces only the same field; an explicit
`None` loss update marks it unknown, while omitted fields retain their current
values. Group overrides target exact recorded group IDs and unknown IDs fail.
Reanalysis never selects contribution patches or changes the underlying
geometry or field evidence.

Palace's native configuration writes `LossTan=0.0` when the user did not
provide a loss tangent because that is the backend-compatible config value.
That native value does not turn an unknown assumption into a known zero: the
Palace v2 index and detached EPR result preserve `loss_tangent=None`, and
SCGSim's analysis keeps the inverse-Q contribution unavailable. A native
infinite-Q or zero-loss display is not evidence that the loss is known to be
zero. The selected Palace candidate retains only native Eigenmode `eig.csv`
`Q=+inf` as explicitly reported native infinity, with its finite Q-based view
unavailable. This preserves what the solver reported without supplying a
physical lossless inference. The [Palace native Q contract](specs/palace-eigenmode.qmd#native-eigenmode-q)
owns the allowance; EPR still uses actual energy/frequency evidence and its
recorded loss assumptions, independently of that native Q value.

Historical Palace surface-film records before
`scgsim.palace.surface-film.v2` can contain a recorded `loss_tangent=0.0`
whose origin is ambiguous. SCGSim retains that raw value in
`recorded_native_assumptions`, but treats the effective loss tangent as unknown
and marks its provenance `historical_ambiguous_zero`. Detached EPR results
preserve both the recorded value and that interpretation; the inverse-Q
contribution remains unavailable.

The `show_epr` figure layout, owner labels, coverage counts, and baseline
inverse-Q subtotal are specified in the [Unified Report Model](report-model.qmd#eigenmode-epr-presentation).
The subtotal is not total device loss or a lifetime estimate; requested mask
rows are alternatives and are not added into it. Sidewall terms remain
uncomputed where they were not evaluated.

`show_epr()` keeps its three-region surface/bulk/junction view.
`plot_epr_result()` returns one adaptive-history figure with independent
frequency, participation, and energy subplots; a valid partial-row frequency
does not fill its unavailable EPR quantities. Both views use stable scientific
keys for selection rather than readable display labels.

## Read the quantities in a real result

Use [offline EPR](course/offline-epr.qmd) for mode/pass selection and attributed
assumption changes on actual recorded results. It exports figures from evidence,
not example numbers. The [report contract](report-model.qmd) owns visible
coverage and ordering; native saved-field requirements live in the
[AEDT contract](specs/aedt-runtime.qmd). Missing channels and unknown loss remain
limitations on interpretation, not zero contributions.
